On the right side there is a load resistor labeled R, and the lower end of the load returns to the neutral line N through the lower wire, therefore this is a three-phase four-wire three-phase half-wave rectifier structure. Reasoning: The problem statement gives the power supply frequency as 400 Hz, and the circuit is a three-phase half-wave rectifier. In a three-phase half-wave rectifier, the three phases successively provide the rectified output in each AC cycle, therefore the output ripple has 3 pulses in each input cycle. Ripple frequency = 3 × 400 Hz = 1200 Hz.

method.method_draft: Describe the image as a diode-OR connection from phases R, Y, and B to the load, with neutral return N. Read from the text that the three-phase source is symmetrical and has frequency 400 Hz. Model the output as the upper envelope of the three phase-to-neutral sinusoids, because the diode attached to the most positive phase conducts. Since the phases are 120 degrees apart, the same output segment repeats after every 120 electrical degrees, i.e. three times per 400 Hz cycle. Therefore the ripple frequency is 3 × 400 = 1200 Hz.
